  CONTEXT. Repository /home/user/threadgame holds "Wishweave Wonders" Level 1: a mobile 2.5D runner (plain JavaScript classic scripts on globalThis.WW, Canvas 2D, no build step) packaged in an Android WebView host (android/). The player's Purl (coral/red crochet ball, one curled tuft) races the computer rival Loop (teal, two loop tufts). The current game draws a sequence of painted 841x1870 "plates" with a 2D camera dolly; between plates a "connector" segment shows a blurred tower-column wipe while Purl runs with no floor. The user now supplied a "Connected World" kit at /home/user/threadgame/kit/connected/Wishweave-Connected-World-Kit (read START-HERE.txt, CLAUDIA-PROMPT.txt, docs/*.txt first) asking for ONE continuous connected 3D course (scenery/level1-connected-layout.glb blockout + scenery/route.json), natural controllable running (auto-run, swipe left/right steer/branch, swipe up jump, double-tap brake toggle, buttons), a smooth chase camera, Loop as an independent rival, and to keep useful existing rules (three threads, Snagling hit/drop/recovery, butterfly, flower-gate finish, one forgiving opening pull lesson, locked cash-out placeholder). For each character set: poses available, canvas sizes, alpha edge quality (halo/fringe? matte color? measure: fraction of semi-transparent edge pixels, any non-premultiplied dark/white fringe), where the feet/ground contact is (bottom-most opaque row per pose, horizontal foot centre), scale consistency between poses (body width in px), whether any side or 3/4 views exist. Compare with the runtime atlases already in the game (game/assets/atlas/*.webp, game/src/data/asset-data.js frames) — are the kit images identical sources?
  2. Measure from the three targets: character on-screen height as a fraction of the 1870 px frame, horizontal position, camera height/pitch impression, road width relative to character width (estimate meters if a character is ~0.9 m tall), border/rope details, colors (sample hex colors of the coral carpet, gold rope rim, teal banner, wood tower, sky), and the HUD layout (does it match the existing HUD in game/index.html/style.css?).
  3. Recommendation: a rigged/procedural 3D Purl and Loop (e.g. crochet-textured sphere body, felt-soled feet, arm nubs, tuft(s)) vs directional sprites. Given only rear + front views exist, what would a directional-sprite approach lack? If 3D, describe how to keep the approved identity (proportions measured from the sprites: body diameter vs foot size, arm nub size/position, tuft shape and size, sole color, knit texture scale) — give numbers. Suggest how to derive a tileable knit texture (procedural canvas V-stitch pattern vs cropping from the sprites) and sample the body base colors (hex) for Purl and Loop.
  4. Which images are usable as textures or billboards in a 3D world: carpet-flat (top-down? tileable?), carpet-rolled, spools (coral/teal/golden-thread) as billboards, swinging-tassel, flower-gate, cover-post, butterfly frames, stitch-loop, Snagling frames. Note perspective/orientation problems.
  Save any contact sheets you make under /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-threadgame/131a49c9-f445-5dda-9dd9-fdcc5c2be76a/scratchpad/inspect/ and list their paths. Return a structured markdown report with concrete numbers.
